title: Hygiene and Sanitation in Food Service — Contamination, Waste, Pests and Personnel
shortDescription: Sources of contamination, cleaning and sanitising, waste disposal, pest and rodent control and personnel hygiene.
genZNote: Most outbreaks start with hands, hot-holding or hidden pests. Hygiene chapter = the boring bits that prevent the dramatic headlines.

sections.heading: Sources of Contamination and Control
bullets: Sources: raw materials, people, air, water, equipment, pests, packaging, cross-contamination between raw and cooked.

Control: colour-coded boards/knives, separation of raw and ready-to-eat, one-way flow, potable water, cleaning-in-place, correct temperature (cold ≤ 5 °C; hot ≥ 60 °C; danger zone ~5–60 °C), FIFO/FEFO stock rotation.

Cleaning vs sanitising vs disinfection: clean removes soil; sanitise reduces microbes to safe levels (chlorine, quaternary ammonium, peracetic acid, hot water ≥ 82 °C); verify with swabs or ATP tests.

sections.heading: Waste Disposal and Pest Control
bullets: Waste: covered bins, frequent removal, separate wet/dry/hazardous, drain traps, composting; used cooking oil to authorised RUCO collectors.

Pests: flies, cockroaches, rodents, birds, stored-product insects. Integrated Pest Management: prevention (proofing, hygiene), monitoring (traps, fly killers), physical control (air curtains, screens), chemical control only by licensed operators with records and no food contact.
Rodent control: seal entry points, baiting stations, keep stores off floor.

sections.heading: Personnel Hygiene
bullets: Handwashing: wet, soap, scrub ~20 seconds, rinse, dry with disposable towel; after toilet, handling raw food, waste or phones.
Clean uniforms, hair covering, no jewellery, nails short; gloves are not a substitute for handwashing.
Medical fitness: annual medical examination and vaccination (e.g. typhoid) for food handlers per FSSAI Schedule 4; exclusion of staff with diarrhoea, vomiting, jaundice, infected wounds.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Hygiene and sanitation in food service combine cross-contamination control, cleaning, pest and waste management and strict personnel hygiene to prevent foodborne illness.

commonTraps: Do not rely on gloves alone.
